study_identification_part.si4_title: Distinct Neurodevelopmental Patterns and Intermediate Integration-Based Predictive Modeling in Autism Spectral Disorder

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize distinct developmental patterns of cortical morphology (CT, SA, GV) in individuals with ASD across the lifespan using normative modeling, identify important neural biomarkers for ASD diagnostics, and develop a deep-learning workflow (LMFGCN) combining graph convolutional networks with low-rank multi-modal tensor fusion for ASD classification.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief:
Answer: ASD exhibits distinct cortical developmental trajectories with early brain overgrowth (0-8 years) driven by increased surface area rather than cortical thickness, converging with TD around age 8-10 years then declining; largely non-overlapping regional CT and SA abnormalities were identified; LMFGCN achieved 81.77% classification accuracy, outperforming traditional methods.
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: Key findings are clearly summarized in the results and discussion sections.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed:
Answer: GAMLSS modeling revealed age-related cortical thinning across the lifespan in both ASD and TD, with ASD showing thinner cortical thickness but larger total surface area and gray matter volume during ages 0-8 years. Growth curves intersect around 8-10 years (termed 'pseudonormalization'), followed by near-linear decrease. Regional analyses showed ASD had thinner CT in sensory-motor cortex (left precentral, right postcentral, paracentral, caudal middle frontal, opercularis) and parahippocampal regions, but thicker CT in left medial orbitofrontal, rostral middle frontal, right lingual, and bilateral lateral occipital regions. For SA, ASD showed decreases in right medial orbitofrontal and bilateral rostral anterior cingulate and lateral orbitofrontal regions, with increases in left isthmus cingulate, transverse temporal, lateral occipital, and bilateral precuneus. GV findings reflected combined CT and SA patterns. The LMFGCN classification model achieved 81.77% accuracy (precision: 82.15%, recall: 81.87%, F1: 81.74%) on the test set using 10-fold cross-validation, significantly outperforming early fusion (74.03%), late fusion (73.48%), traditional GCNs (72.89%), and conventional machine learning methods (SVM: 59.95%, XGBoost: 58.21%, RF: 59.45%).
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: Detailed quantitative results are provided throughout the results section and summarized in tables and figures.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Answer: Novel intermediate integration approach combining modality-specific GCNs with low-rank multimodal tensor fusion (LMFGCN) for ASD classification. Age-specific preprocessing pipelines tailored to developmental stages (Infant FreeSurfer for 0-2 years, ANTs+FreeSurfer with age-specific templates for 3-6 years, standard FreeSurfer for >6 years). Separate normative trajectories modeled for CT, SA, and GV emphasizing their distinct developmental patterns and genetic determinants. Findings support radial unit hypothesis: early SA expansion reflects neuronal progenitor proliferation, while CT reflects later synaptic/columnar changes. Code availability stated at https://github.com/ASD-trajectory-and-classification. Study highlights importance of distinguishing SA from CT for understanding ASD pathobiology during early brain overgrowth period.

Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative

Supporting Text: There are several limitations to the current study. Firstly, current study has a larger sample size cross the life span, but various participating sites and sex differences still be challenging for multi-sits datasets. While we made effects to control for these effects in our models, it cannot fully exclude potential influence. Secondly, the classification model for ASD must be replicated on other independent datasets before any application in clinical decision-making. Lastly, the developmental trajectories for brain changes in ASD are predominantly drawn from our current cross-sectional data, future longitudinal studies with larger sample sizes are essential to clarify reported developmental trajectories and determine whether distinct early developmental trajectories can predict brain changes in the later life.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a preprint published on bioRxiv (not peer-reviewed). The study spans a wide age range (0-64 years) with particular focus on early development (0-8 years). KQJH dataset included very young children (0-6 years) who required sedation with 10% chloral hydrate (50 mg/ml) orally or by enema to reduce head movement. There is a minor discrepancy in the supplementary materials regarding KQJH exclusions: text states 59 inaccurately segmented scans but also states 107 participants were excluded; the final sample size confirms 107 is the correct exclusion count (323 original - 107 excluded = 216 ASD + 48 TD = 264 final). The study uses sex-stratified analyses in some contexts but does not report separate normative models by sex. Year-by-year brain templates (16 years) were obtained from Zhi Yang (https://osf.io/fm7cq/). Total sample after QA: 2,009 participants (1,011 ASD, 998 TD) from 37 sites (17 ABIDE-I + 19 ABIDE-II + 1 KQJH). The study represents one of the largest ASD neuroimaging studies spanning the lifespan with age-appropriate preprocessing. Classification focus is on supervised learning rather than semi-supervised approaches used in previous GCN studies.
